[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc3Foundations Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The foundations module contains features related to founding and core beliefs/principles of the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1a", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u26ea Churches", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Churches list holds your church. Once Enable Multi-Church is switched on in Church Features, it can also hold branch or satellite churches: mark the main church Is Group, then add each branch with the main church as its Parent Church. There is always exactly one main church (the one without a parent).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1website01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What each church shows on the public website. Tick Publish to put the church on the site, then fill in:
- About and Mission Statement, which its About Us page uses
- Image, a photo or logo for its card on the Locations page
- Address, Phone and Email, which the footer and the Contact Us page use
Leave Phone or Email blank and the church shows whatever is in Contact Us Settings, which is shared by the whole site. The Website manual covers how visitors move between locations.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1print001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "These details also print. Anything you print for a branch church, such as a giving statement, carries that church's own name and contact line rather than the main church's. Legal Name and Tax ID work differently: leave them blank on a branch and it prints the main church's, because the main church is usually the registered charity that issues the receipt.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In multi-church mode every church-specific record (Person, Family, Prayer Request, Function, Fund, Collection, Bulletin and so on) gains a Church field, shown near the top of the form and as a standard list filter. New records default to the church of the person saving them. Records that belong to another record (a sign-up to its function, a care request to its person) take that record's church automatically, and a family belongs to the church of its head of household. You can add such a record only for a record of your own church or a shared one: you cannot book another church's room, move money out of its fund, or record a care request, an alms request or a prayer for its people. The Church Directory still lists a family under every branch that has one of its members. Single-church sites never see the field.

Some records can be handed to every church instead of being kept by one. These carry a Shared with all churches tick box: songs, sermons, sermon series and handouts, vendors, rooms, locations and assets, the occasions churches hold together, which are functions and meeting minutes, and the two things money runs through, funds and ministries. Sharing is one record at a time, never a whole type: nothing is shared until somebody ticks the box on that record. Tick it and every church can see and use it, whichever church shared it, and the Church field disappears because the record no longer belongs to one.

Shared By on the record names the church that shared it, and you can filter a list by it to separate what you shared from what was shared with you. Open a record another church shared and a note at the top says so, with the tick box locked.

Only the church that shared a record can stop sharing it, or delete it. Untick the box there and the record goes back to that church and leaves everyone else's lists, and anything attached to it, such as a booking of a shared room, goes back with it. A branch that no longer wants something shared with it has to ask the church that shared it, so one branch cannot take a resource away from the rest. Anything attached to a shared record is shared along with it, such as a booking of a shared room or a sign-up to a shared function, so every church sees the same diary and the same list of names. Gifts and expenses are never shared: each one keeps the church that gave or spent it, so every report shows a church only its own money. A shared fund or ministry therefore shows its joint figures to every church that can see it: the fund's balance and list of transactions, the ministry's running total of what has been spent on it. People and attendance are never shared.

A Budget tracks the spending of its own church. Tick Include Branch Churches on it to count what the churches beneath it spend as well, which is how the main church budgets for everyone at once.

The Church record also holds the church's Mission Statement and a Church Verse (a Bible Reference). It can also carry an Image, such as a logo. Bulletins print the verse on the back cover and the image on the front cover when the Church Verse and Church Image sections are switched on. The Church Directory prints the verse on its cover, and the image as well when Church Image on Cover is ticked. Bulletins and the Church Directory cover print the Website. A branch that leaves Legal Name, Tax ID, Default Bible Translation or Website blank uses its parent's.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1f", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Turning Enable Multi-Church on stamps the main church on every existing record and gives every existing user a permission for the main church with branches hidden, so nothing becomes visible to anyone by accident. It cannot be turned off again while branch churches exist.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1d", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who Sees Which Church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Everyone sees the records of their own church, and nothing from the others. Someone at a branch sees that branch's events, prayer requests and giving. The main church's records stay out of their way, and theirs stay out of the main church's.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1dir1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "One people directory", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1dir2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People and families are the exception. Every church can look up every Person and Family, so a branch can find a visitor from the main church, choose a main-church pastor as a counselor or speaker, or check in a family from another campus. The Church field on each person shows which church they belong to.
- Only a person's own church can change them. Another church sees the form as read-only.
- Only a person's own church can add a Background Check, Care Request, Care Assignment or Visitation Log for them. You can open a Follow-up Card only on a Follow-up Workflow of your own church. A workflow that starts by itself, such as on a first check-in, still opens a card for a visitor from another church.
- To move someone to another church, use a Member Transfer.
- Prayer requests, care, counseling, visitation and giving stay with each church, whichever directory setting you use. One exception while the directory is shared: finance and care staff of another church can see a person's Giving and Care figures in lists, reports and exports, but not on the Person form. Check-In, People Editor and Church Manager users of every church can also read a person's Medical Notes. To keep all of these inside each church, tick Keep People and Families Private to Each Church.

To hide each church's people and families from the other churches, tick Keep People and Families Private to Each Church in Church Features. The Check-In Station still finds everyone at a function that is shared with all churches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Where a person's church comes from", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "From the Church field on their Person record. Fill that in, link them to a login (the Invite to Portal button does this for you), and they can see that church and no other. There is nothing else to set up.
If they later move to another church, change the same field, or confirm a Member Transfer with a To Church. What they can see moves with them.
A staff login is different. Linking it to a person by hand does not change its churches, so set them in User Permission. A later change of the person's Church field, or a Member Transfer, still moves them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People who belong to one church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Most people. They never have to choose a church, so the app stops asking: the Church field is hidden on their forms, the Church filter is hidden on their lists and reports, and anything they create belongs to their church automatically.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Seeing the branches as well", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Someone at a church that has branches beneath it still sees only their own church to begin with. To bring the branches in, choose Include Branch Churches from the menu at the top left. While the branches are included:
- a blue note sits at the top of every page, so nobody forgets they are looking at more than their own church
- that same menu item now reads Hide Branch Churches, which puts things back
- lists and reports gain a Church box. Leave it empty to see every church at once, or pick one church to see only that church.
- ticking Expand filters to branches on the blue note changes that last point: picking a church then shows its branches too. This is remembered for that person alone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People who see everything", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Two kinds of account: the built-in Administrator, which the app never restricts, and anyone who has not been given a church. Their reports still open on the main church, so clear the Church box to see every church at once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1share1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Assigning and sharing", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1share2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With more than one church, you can assign a record (Assign To) or share it only with someone who can see that record's church. Assigning it to anyone else stops with a message, because the assignment would let them read a record of another church. A record of one church cannot be shared with everyone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e10", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If someone sees the wrong thing", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e11", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Check the Church field on their Person record first, since that is what drives everything else. What it creates behind the scenes is a User Permission, which an administrator can look at or change there directly. A change made by hand stays until that person's church or login changes, at which point it is set again from their Person record.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fQeaH6cwov", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Note: Without multi-church, only one Church record is allowed. With it, only one main church (a church without a Parent Church) is allowed; every other church must have a Parent Church that is marked Is Group.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w8oEjl0tNc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcd4Beliefs", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rx8sNKF0oc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Beliefs are the foundational principles the church stands for.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nVhOr1yDL4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding church beliefs, note the following:
- Type the Bible references each belief rests on, such as Romans 3:23; Ephesians 2:8-9. They show beneath the statement on the Beliefs web page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetricsH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc8Weekly Metrics", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetrics01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Weekly Metrics keeps one record for each church and each week, in the Summary sidebar. It holds the attendance of the week, the first-time visitors, the active members, the people in groups, the people who serve, and the giving and givers of the week. Churchit writes these records itself every night. You cannot add or change one by hand.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetrics02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each night, Churchit writes this week and counts last week again. So attendance, first-time visitors and giving can change when someone records a late check-in or a late collection. Active members, people in groups and people serving are the counts on the day of the record. Churchit writes them only for the current week, so last week keeps the numbers of its last day.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetrics03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Fill the past year. Open Weekly Metrics and click Fill the Last 52 Weeks. Only Church Manager and System Manager users see this button. It fills attendance, first-time visitors and giving for the weeks before last week, and the nightly job writes last week. A week that had no record before shows 0 for members, groups and serving, because Churchit cannot know those numbers for the past. A week that had a record keeps its numbers.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetrics04", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What the numbers count. Attendance adds the attendance of each function that starts in the week. A function that is shared with all churches counts one time, for the church that shared it. The schedule of a repeating function does not count. Giving adds every submitted collection of the week, the same total as the Weekly Giving chart. It includes sign-up and form payments and refunds. Givers counts each person who gave in the week one time.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetrics05", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Only Church Finance, Church Manager and System Manager users see the giving numbers. Church Staff see the other numbers. The Summary workspace shows the Attendance by Week chart, and Church Finance and Church Manager users also see the Giving by Week chart. If you change the first day of the week in System Settings, new records start on the new day, and the weeks before and after the change overlap.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udd17Send records to other systems", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This part is for a System Manager. Churchit can send a record to another system when someone adds or changes it, for example to a mailing tool or a chat room. You do not need custom code.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Send a record with a Webhook", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook04", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open Webhooks and add one:
- Set DocType to the record to send, such as Person, Function Sign-Up or Connection Card. Set Doc Event to when it goes, such as after_insert for a new record.
- Set Request URL to the address that the other system gives you.
- Tick Enable Security and type a Webhook Secret. Give the same secret to the other system. Each request then carries a signature in the X-Frappe-Webhook-Signature header, so the other system can check that the request came from your site.
- Set Request Structure to JSON. In JSON Request Body, put only the fields that the other system needs, for example {\"first_name\": \"{{ doc.first_name }}\", \"email\": \"{{ doc.email }}\"}.
- With more than one church, type doc.church == \"CHURCH-ID\" in Condition, with the ID of the church from its Church record. Then only that church's records go.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook05", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Send an alert to a chat room", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook06", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Frappe sends alerts to Slack. Mattermost and Matrix accept the same alerts:
- In the chat app, make an incoming webhook and copy its address. In Mattermost this is an Incoming Webhook. In Matrix it is a webhook of the hookshot bridge.
- Open Slack Webhook URL, add one with a Name, and paste the address in Webhook URL.
- Open Notifications and add one. Set Channel to Slack, choose the Slack Webhook URL in Slack Channel, and set Document Type, Send Alert On and Message.
- With more than one church, type doc.church == \"CHURCH-ID\" in Condition.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook07", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Note: Never send care, medical, pickup or giving fields to another system, in a Webhook or in an alert. The other system does not protect them as Churchit does.", "col": 12}}]
